# Wellness Recovery Center of New Jersey

> Wellness Recovery Center of New Jersey is an accredited addiction and mental health treatment center in West Windsor, NJ, offering partial hospitalization (PHP), intensive outpatient (IOP), mental health IOP, outpatient and dual diagnosis care.

Address: 231 Clarksville Road, Suite 1, West Windsor, NJ 08550. Phone: (866) 861-3449 · info@wellnessrecoverynj.com. Canonical site: https://www.wellnessrecoverynj.com/

## Treatment Programs

- [Treatment Programs](https://www.wellnessrecoverynj.com/treatment): Explore our full continuum of outpatient addiction and mental health treatment in New Jersey — PHP, IOP, Outpatient, Mental Health IOP, and Dual Diagnosis care.
- [Dual Diagnosis Treatment in New Jersey](https://www.wellnessrecoverynj.com/treatment/dual-diagnosis): Addiction and mental health struggles are deeply intertwined. Our dual-diagnosis program addresses substance use and co-occurring mental health conditions at the same time — because treating one without the other rarely lasts.
- [Intensive Outpatient Program in New Jersey](https://www.wellnessrecoverynj.com/treatment/intensive-outpatient-program): We offer flexible intensive outpatient treatment designed around our clients’ needs, with continued care and support. IOP delivers meaningful clinical structure while allowing you to keep up with work, school, and family responsibilities.
- [Mental Health IOP in New Jersey](https://www.wellnessrecoverynj.com/treatment/mental-health-iop): A structured Mental Health IOP in NJ for anxiety, depression, and trauma that fits your daily routine. When symptoms begin interfering with daily life, there is often a middle ground between weekly therapy and inpatient treatment — and this is it.
- [Outpatient Program in New Jersey](https://www.wellnessrecoverynj.com/treatment/outpatient): Our standard outpatient program provides continued care and accountability for clients who have built a solid foundation in recovery and are ready for a lighter, sustainable level of support.
- [Partial Hospitalization Program in New Jersey](https://www.wellnessrecoverynj.com/treatment/partial-hospitalization): Our Partial Hospitalization Program offers the benefits of inpatient treatment without the 24/7 stay at a residential facility. PHP delivers the highest level of structured, clinically intensive care we offer on an outpatient basis.

## What We Treat

- [What We Treat](https://www.wellnessrecoverynj.com/what-we-treat): Expert, judgment-free treatment for alcohol, opioids, benzodiazepines, cocaine, heroin, fentanyl, meth, oxycodone, prescription drugs, and Xanax addiction in New Jersey.
- [Alcohol Rehab in New Jersey](https://www.wellnessrecoverynj.com/what-we-treat/alcohol): Because alcohol is socially accepted and everywhere we go, recovery comes with unique challenges — bars, restaurants, and gatherings can all be triggers. Our program teaches the coping skills and support systems you need to navigate stress and stay grounded in sobriety.
- [Benzo Rehab in New Jersey](https://www.wellnessrecoverynj.com/what-we-treat/benzo): Roughly 19% of U.S. adults experience an anxiety disorder each year, and benzodiazepines are among the most commonly prescribed treatments. Effective recovery combines careful medical support with therapy that addresses the anxiety underneath.
- [Cocaine Rehab in New Jersey](https://www.wellnessrecoverynj.com/what-we-treat/cocaine): Cocaine is a powerful Schedule II stimulant, and its short-lived high drives a cycle of repeated use. When mixed with opioids like fentanyl, the risk of fatal overdose rises sharply.
- [Fentanyl Rehab in New Jersey](https://www.wellnessrecoverynj.com/what-we-treat/fentanyl): Fentanyl has become a driving force behind the opioid crisis. Fifty to one hundred times stronger than morphine, it’s often mixed into other drugs without the user’s knowledge — making overdose a constant danger.
- [Heroin Rehab in New Jersey](https://www.wellnessrecoverynj.com/what-we-treat/heroin): Heroin addiction often grows out of costly prescription-opioid dependence, and it can bring profound chaos to a person’s life. With proper treatment and genuine support, lasting recovery is absolutely within reach.
- [Meth Rehab in New Jersey](https://www.wellnessrecoverynj.com/what-we-treat/meth): Meth addiction affects millions of Americans, and stigma too often keeps people from getting help. We meet you with compassion, not judgment — and with a full program built for lasting recovery.
- [Opioid Rehab in New Jersey](https://www.wellnessrecoverynj.com/what-we-treat/opioids): The opioid epidemic has made overdose one of the leading causes of injury-related death in the United States. Our program meets it with a client-first philosophy and a full continuum of care — from partial hospitalization to outpatient services.
- [Oxycodone Rehab in New Jersey](https://www.wellnessrecoverynj.com/what-we-treat/oxycodone): Oxycodone (OxyContin, Percocet) is a Schedule II opioid with high addiction and overdose risk. Many people begin with a legitimate prescription and, as dependence grows, move toward cheaper opioids like heroin and fentanyl.
- [Prescription Drug Rehab in New Jersey](https://www.wellnessrecoverynj.com/what-we-treat/prescription-drugs): Prescription medications help millions manage pain, anxiety, and ADHD — but controlled substances carry real addiction risk. Misuse can be unintentional or intentional, and it often begins as an attempt to self-medicate emotional distress.
- [Xanax Rehab in New Jersey](https://www.wellnessrecoverynj.com/what-we-treat/xanax): Xanax (alprazolam) is a Schedule IV benzodiazepine prescribed for anxiety, panic, and sleep. Its abuse risk is lower than higher-scheduled drugs, but it still poses genuine physical and psychological dependence — and stopping abruptly can be dangerous.

## Admissions & Insurance

- [Admissions & Insurance](https://www.wellnessrecoverynj.com/admissions): Navigating insurance should never be a barrier to care. Verify your benefits for free — we work with most major private and commercial insurance carriers on an out-of-network basis.
- [Contact Us](https://www.wellnessrecoverynj.com/contact): Get in touch with Wellness Recovery Center of New Jersey. Same-day admissions, transportation available, and 24/7 help and support. Call (866) 861-3449.
- [Frequently Asked Questions](https://www.wellnessrecoverynj.com/faq): Answers to common questions about treatment, insurance, admissions, and what to expect at Wellness Recovery Center of New Jersey.
- [Tour Our Facilities](https://www.wellnessrecoverynj.com/tour): Take a tour of Wellness Recovery Center of New Jersey — a modern, secluded, and innovative treatment facility in West Windsor, NJ designed for comfort and healing.

## About

- [Who We Are](https://www.wellnessrecoverynj.com/about): Wellness Recovery Center of New Jersey is an addiction treatment center rooted in client-centered care. Learn about our mission, values, and expert clinical team.
- [Amy Baisden — Lead Clinical Therapist](https://www.wellnessrecoverynj.com/about/amy-baisden): Amy Baisden is a Licensed Marriage and Family Therapist and EMDR-trained clinician who works with adults navigating trauma, grief and loss, depression, anxiety, attachment wounds, life transitions, and recovery. She earned her Master’s degree in Marriage and Family Therapy from Touro University and brings extensive experience in community mental health, non profit settings and partial hospitalization/intensive outpatient settings, supporting individuals with co-occurring mental health and substance use disorders. Amy also has a strong background in crisis management, as well as grief and loss work, with a particular focus on complex family dynamics.
- [Anthony Paccillo — Client Relations Liaison](https://www.wellnessrecoverynj.com/about/anthony-paccillo): Anthony Paccillo serves as the Client Relations Liaison at Wellness Recovery Center New Jersey, where he is dedicated to creating a welcoming, supportive experience for clients and their families throughout the treatment journey. He works closely with admissions, clinical, and operations teams to ensure clients feel informed, connected, and supported from their first interaction through their transition into ongoing recovery. Prior to joining Wellness Recovery Center, Anthony gained hands-on experience working directly with clients in the behavioral healthcare field while collaborating with multidisciplinary teams and community partners to strengthen engagement and improve the overall client experience.
- [Christina Lilly — Office Manager](https://www.wellnessrecoverynj.com/about/christina-lilly): Christina Lilly serves as the Office Manager at Wellness Recovery Center, where she plays a vital role in ensuring the day-to-day operations of the facility run smoothly and efficiently. Since joining the team in 2024, Christina has become a central point of support for all departments, helping to maintain organization, communication, and overall workflow across the organization. In her role, Christina oversees administrative operations, coordinates office procedures, and provides ongoing support to clinical, case management, and leadership teams.
- [Danielle Foreman — Case Manager](https://www.wellnessrecoverynj.com/about/danielle-foreman): Danielle Foreman is a Case Manager at Wellness Recovery Center of New Jersey who is committed to helping individuals navigate the recovery process with compassion, encouragement, and personalized support. With more than eight years of experience in the behavioral health field, she works closely with clients to help them access resources, overcome challenges, and build a strong foundation for lasting recovery. Danielle believes every individual has the capacity for growth and positive change when provided with the right guidance, support, and opportunities.
- [Deanna Koester — Case Manager](https://www.wellnessrecoverynj.com/about/deanna-koester): Deanna Koester is a Case Manager at Wellness Recovery Center of New Jersey who is passionate about helping individuals navigate their recovery journey with compassion, encouragement, and personalized support. Drawing on her background in mental health and substance use recovery, she is committed to creating a safe, welcoming environment where clients feel seen, heard, and empowered to make meaningful progress. Currently pursuing a degree in Social Work, Deanna continues to expand her knowledge and clinical skills to better serve individuals and families affected by behavioral health and substance use disorders.
- [Dylan Kuzinski — Medical Liaison](https://www.wellnessrecoverynj.com/about/dylan-kuzinski): Dylan Kuzinski serves as the Medical Liaison at Wellness Recovery Center of New Jersey, where he plays a key role in facilitating clear and effective communication between clients and medical providers to ensure continuity of care. In his role, Dylan oversees medication orders and coordinates timely delivery, helping clients receive the treatment they need without delay. With over five years of experience in the field, including one year in his current position, Dylan brings both knowledge and dedication to his work.
- [Ila Holgerson — Director of Operations](https://www.wellnessrecoverynj.com/about/ila-holgerson): Ila Holgerson serves as the Director of Operations at Wellness Recovery Center, where she has been a dedicated member of the team since 2023. Originally from Gilbert, Arizona, she brings a compassionate, client-centered approach to leadership and a strong commitment to creating an environment where individuals feel supported throughout their recovery journey.
- [Jaclyn Paradise — Clinical Therapist](https://www.wellnessrecoverynj.com/about/jaclyn-paradise): Jaclyn Paradise is a Licensed Professional Counselor (LPC) and Certified Trauma Professional who works with adults navigating trauma, anxiety, life transitions, and recovery. She earned her master’s degree in Clinical Mental Health Counseling from Rider University and has extensive experience in both private practice and intensive outpatient settings, supporting individuals with co-occurring mental health and substance use challenges. Jaclyn’s approach is holistic and trauma-informed, integrating parts work, mindfulness, and body-based practices to help clients reconnect with themselves and feel safe in their own bodies.
- [Jordan Kane — Group Facilitator](https://www.wellnessrecoverynj.com/about/jordan-kane): Since earning my Bachelor’s degree in Recreational Therapy from Temple University in 2018, I have been working as a Certified Therapeutic Recreation Specialist (CTRS) in a variety of behavioral health settings. My experience includes both inpatient and outpatient care, where I have facilitated group therapy focused on supporting individuals in their mental health and substance use recovery journeys. I am passionate about integrating leisure education, team-building activities, journaling, and horticulture-based interventions into my groups to promote self-expression, coping skills, and overall well-being.
- [Julie Mitchell — Alumni Coordinator](https://www.wellnessrecoverynj.com/about/julie-mitchell): Julie Mitchell is passionate about supporting individuals as they continue their recovery journey beyond treatment, helping alumni build meaningful connections, strengthen their support systems, and maintain long-term wellness. As Alumni Coordinator, she is dedicated to fostering a strong recovery community where individuals feel encouraged, supported, and empowered to thrive in their everyday lives. Julie earned her Bachelor of Science in Psychology from the New York Institute of Technology and her Master of Arts in Addiction Counseling from the Hazelden Betty Ford Graduate School of Addiction Studies, a nationally recognized leader in addiction treatment education.
- [Kimberly Cotterell — Group Facilitator](https://www.wellnessrecoverynj.com/about/kimberly-cotterell): Kim is a 200-hour Registered Yoga Teacher (RYT) with additional training in mobility, Yoga Nidra, Reiki Level II, and somatic methods. ## Areas We Serve

- [Areas We Serve](https://www.wellnessrecoverynj.com/areas-we-serve): From our West Windsor facility, Wellness Recovery Center serves communities across central and northern New Jersey — Mercer, Hunterdon, Somerset, Morris, Sussex, and Warren counties.
- [Hunterdon County Drug & Alcohol Rehab](https://www.wellnessrecoverynj.com/areas-we-serve/hunterdon-county): Compassionate, evidence-based drug and alcohol treatment for Flemington, Raritan, Clinton, and the wider Hunterdon County community.
- [Mercer County Drug & Alcohol Rehab](https://www.wellnessrecoverynj.com/areas-we-serve/mercer-county): Serving Trenton, Hamilton, Ewing, and the surrounding communities, our nearby facility provides customized addiction and mental health treatment for all of Mercer County.
- [Morris County Drug & Alcohol Rehab](https://www.wellnessrecoverynj.com/areas-we-serve/morris-county): Individualized outpatient care for Morristown, Parsippany, Roxbury, Dover, Mount Olive, and the greater Morris County area.
- [Somerset County Drug & Alcohol Rehab](https://www.wellnessrecoverynj.com/areas-we-serve/somerset-county): Specialized addiction treatment for Franklin, Bridgewater, Somerville, North Plainfield, and communities throughout Somerset County.
- [Sussex County Drug & Alcohol Rehab](https://www.wellnessrecoverynj.com/areas-we-serve/sussex-county): Flexible, confidential treatment for Newton, Sparta, Vernon, Hopatcong, Wantage, and the Sussex County community.
- [Warren County Drug & Alcohol Rehab](https://www.wellnessrecoverynj.com/areas-we-serve/warren-county): Free, confidential assessments and personalized outpatient treatment for Phillipsburg, Hackettstown, Washington, Blairstown, and Warren County.

## Blog

- [Adventure Therapy: Overcoming Fears and Building Confidence in Recovery](https://www.wellnessrecoverynj.com/blog/adventure-therapy): Adventure therapy pairs outdoor activities with psychotherapy to strengthen physical, psychological, social, and spiritual well-being in recovery.
- [How a Mental Health IOP Can Help You Build Stability Without Leaving Home](https://www.wellnessrecoverynj.com/blog/benefits-of-mental-health-iop): A Mental Health IOP offers a middle ground between weekly therapy and inpatient care — structured support several times a week while you keep living your life.
- [Discovering Purpose and Meaning in Life After Addiction](https://www.wellnessrecoverynj.com/blog/discovering-purpose-and-meaning-in-life-after-addiction-a-guide-to-wellness-recovery-nj): Finding purpose after overcoming addiction is a deeply personal journey — through self-reflection, clarifying values, setting goals, and contributing to community.
- [Understanding Different Treatment Modalities for Recovery](https://www.wellnessrecoverynj.com/blog/exploring-different-treatment-modalities): Understanding the full range of treatment approaches is crucial to overcoming addiction — each modality offers distinct benefits and can be personalized to the individual.
- [How Addiction Affects Families and Relationships](https://www.wellnessrecoverynj.com/blog/how-addiction-affects-families-and-relationships): Addiction is a disease that reaches far beyond the individual, affecting the entire family system — and family therapy can help repair the damage.
- [How Alcohol Addiction Can Gradually Take Over Daily Life](https://www.wellnessrecoverynj.com/blog/how-alcohol-addiction-affects-daily-life): Alcohol dependence rarely happens overnight. Understanding the gradual changes can help you recognize when support may be needed.
- [How a Partial Hospitalization Program Helps During Early Recovery](https://www.wellnessrecoverynj.com/blog/how-php-helps-early-recovery): PHP provides structured, full-day treatment with the accountability and clinical support that early recovery demands.
- [How to Help a Loved One Battling Addiction](https://www.wellnessrecoverynj.com/blog/how-to-help-a-loved-one-battling-addiction): Watching someone you love struggle with addiction is painful — but your steady support can be the deciding factor in their long-term recovery.
- [Why Xanax Addiction Can Develop Faster Than People Expect](https://www.wellnessrecoverynj.com/blog/how-xanax-addiction-develops): Though Xanax is commonly prescribed for anxiety, it carries a high risk of dependence — and many people are surprised by how quickly their bodies come to rely on it.
- [Mental Health Treatment in New Jersey](https://www.wellnessrecoverynj.com/blog/mental-health-treatment-new-jersey): Mental health challenges can strain relationships and undermine work — but effective, personalized professional treatment is available.
- [Mental Health Treatment in New Jersey: Flexible Care That Fits Your Life](https://www.wellnessrecoverynj.com/blog/mental-health-treatment-new-jersey-2): Outpatient programs in New Jersey provide structured mental health support while letting people keep up with work, family, and personal responsibilities.
- [New Year, New Routine: How IOP Helps You Build Stability in Early Recovery](https://www.wellnessrecoverynj.com/blog/new-year-new-routine-how-iop-helps-you-build-stability-in-early-recovery): An Intensive Outpatient Program delivers structured support during early recovery while letting you keep up with work, family, and daily life.
- [Opioid Withdrawal Symptoms: Timeline, Risks, and What to Expect](https://www.wellnessrecoverynj.com/blog/opioid-withdrawal-symptoms): Quitting opioids triggers withdrawal symptoms that are intensely uncomfortable but usually not life-threatening. Understanding the timeline helps people prepare for recovery.
- [The Role of Therapy in Addiction Recovery](https://www.wellnessrecoverynj.com/blog/role-of-therapy-in-addiction-recovery): No two people experience addiction the same way, so therapy must be tailored to the individual. Finding the right approach — and sticking with it — is essential to lasting sobriety.
- [Signs of Prescription Drug Abuse in Adults](https://www.wellnessrecoverynj.com/blog/signs-of-prescription-drug-abuse): Prescription drug misuse often develops quietly, which makes it hard to detect. Recognizing the early warning signs allows for intervention before dependency takes hold.
- [Understanding Dual Diagnosis Treatment in New Jersey](https://www.wellnessrecoverynj.com/blog/understanding-dual-diagnosis-treatment-in-new-jersey): Dual diagnosis is the simultaneous presence of a substance use disorder and a mental health condition. Treating them together is essential to prevent relapse.
- [Wellness Recovery Center: Pioneering Holistic Recovery in New Jersey](https://www.wellnessrecoverynj.com/blog/wellness-recovery-center-pioneering-holistic-recovery-in-new-jersey): Comprehensive addiction treatment that pairs medical supervision with holistic therapies, guiding clients toward sustainable recovery and whole-person well-being.
- [What to Expect from Addiction Treatment in West Windsor, New Jersey](https://www.wellnessrecoverynj.com/blog/west-windsor-addiction-treatment-guide): Evidence-based addiction treatment in West Windsor for substance use disorders and co-occurring mental health conditions, with individualized plans for every stage.
- [When Willpower Isn’t Enough: Healing the Hidden Drivers of Addiction](https://www.wellnessrecoverynj.com/blog/when-willpower-isnt-enough-healing-the-hidden-drivers-of-addiction-in-new-jersey): Many people relapse despite strong willpower because untreated anxiety, depression, and trauma quietly drive their substance use. Integrated dual-diagnosis care offers a real path forward.
